pattern_explanation: Both languages borrowed these words from the same Latin roots, so the spellings look alike. Over time the meanings moved apart in Portuguese, so each word now means something different from its English look-alike.
false_friend_warning: Students may think these Portuguese words mean 'actually', 'assist', 'pretend' or 'eventual' because the spelling looks similar, but their real meanings are currently, to watch, to intend and occasional. Check the meaning before translating word for word.
